title: eng-sre
text:
eng-sre

messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT OPENED · KV cache slab-fragmentation causing p99 tail latency surge in us-west-2. Sev: 2. Symptoms: streaming stalls, elevated timeouts. Runbook: https://rwd/internal/runbooks/kv-slab-fragmentation · paging oncall
amanda: ack — oncall responding, pulling metrics now
amanda: quick snapshot (last 5m): p95=220ms p99=2.4s, streaming_stall_count +7x. Several realtime customers report reconnects.
rick: digging into metrics — kv_evictions/sec spiked ~x6 at 15:12 UTC. prefill_queue_depth high; prefill CPU >> decode CPU (prefill 72% vs decode 22% avg on affected nodes).
sanjay: logs show long decode backlog on nodes gpux-3/4; prefill keeps prefetching prefixes causing slab churn and repeated evictions. Prefill is thrashing hot slabs.
amanda: @carlos can you run `kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=kv-cache -o wide` and also `curl prometheus:9090/api/v1/query?query=kv_evictions_total` for last 30m?
carlos: ran checks — 6 kv-cache pods. 4 colocated on nodepool-a (same SKU), two pods show OOMKill events within last hour: pod/kv-cache-3, pod/kv-cache-5. Prom query shows evictions peaked at 1830/s at spike.
emily: suggested mitigations: immediate — reduce PREFILL_WORKERS to 2, increase decode workers by 1 per node, and roll kv-cache pods across nodepools to rebalance slab distribution. Also consider temporary routing of realtime traffic to model-x-small to lower kv footprint.
rick: applying patch to reduce prefill concurrency: `kubectl set env deployment/kv-prefill PREFILL_WORKERS=2 -n inference`
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Patch applied to deployment/kv-prefill at 2026-03-17T15:34:00Z (image unchanged)
sanjay: metrics after patch: prefill_queue_depth down ~60% within 2m, eviction_rate decreasing. p99 improved to ~1.1s but still above SLO (800ms). Streaming stalls reduced but intermittent tails persist.
amanda: doing rolling restart of kv-cache pods on nodepool-a, one at a time to allow slabs to rebalance. Starting with kv-cache-1.
carlos: restarted kv-cache-1; came back healthy. Per-pod occupancy now more even across slabs. No crashloop observed.
emily: routing change applied: traffic tag realtime=true now preferentially hits model-x-small via routing policy, fallback to main model when healthy. Patch pushed to traffic-router.

messages_continued:
rick: routing patch applied. Streaming-stall rate reduced ~4x. p95 ~300ms, p99 ~700ms. Customers reporting substantial improvement; a few still see 1-1.5s tails intermittently.
amanda: Handoff note — I'll hand off to night oncall @sanjay in 20m. Summary for next oncall: root cause is aggressive prefill prefetch/backpressure failure causing slab fragmentation -> high eviction churn -> tail decode/backlog -> streaming stalls. Mitigations executed: PREFILL_WORKERS reduced, decode workers bumped, rolling kv-cache rebalance, temporary routing to lower-footprint model. Followups: permanent slab rebalancer, prefill backpressure + soft limits, ensure nodepool distribution policy, alert thresholds for kv_eviction_rate and prefill_queue_depth.
sanjay: ack. I'll monitor for the next 2 hours and open INF-7232: "Prefill backpressure and slab rebalancer" with priority P1. Will include heap/occupancy histograms and schedule a design review.
emily: added regression alert in console for (kv_eviction_rate > 100/s sustained) and p99 > 800ms for 5m. Tagging product-impact: realtime customers.
amanda: marking incident severity -> downgraded to Sev3 after stabilizing metrics; keeping incident open for postmortem.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED · Severity downgraded to Sev3. Incident will remain open for postmortem and follow-up action items.
